svg.text: S
spawn
C
core
Where enemies walk
One board, three kinds of enemy, three routes. Nobody steers an enemy:
each one takes the cheapest way to the core for its own kind.
Walkers go round
To a walker, a wall tile counts like 15 tiles of walking. Going
round is cheaper here, so they take the long way: about 71 tiles,
past all nine towers. They chew nothing.
Sappers go through
To a sapper, a wall tile counts like 3 tiles. It cuts through the
two walls that are one tile thick (1 and 2), leaves the thick wall
(3) alone, and is there after about 50 tiles, past five towers.
Flyers go straight
A straight line over rocks (4), walls and towers: 44 tiles. Nothing
you build bends it. Only towers that can hit flyers shoot at them;
here one of those is in reach.
Same kind, same entrance, same route.
Enemies of one kind walk in single file along one line. The line is
drawn on the board before the wave, so you can build against it.
The director chooses the kind, never the path.
It decides what comes (and later, from which side). After that every
enemy finds its own way by the rule above. It cannot aim one at a tile.
A route can change in mid-wave.
When a wall is chewed through, or you build, every enemy on the
board works out its way again from where it stands.
Dark blocks: rocks, part of the map. Light tiles: walls the player drew. Rings: towers. The pink and orange routes are what the game's own path rule gives for this board.
